# Workflow

Workflow owns durable multi-step processes, approval, waiting, retry and resume.
Use one transactional Handler for atomic work that does not wait.

## Compact V3 graph

```json
{
  "workflows": {
    "refund_approval": {
      "enabled": true,
      "run_as": "refund_manager",
      "trigger": {"type": "manual"},
      "action": {"type": "workflow_graph"},
      "trigger_contract": {"type": "manual", "object_key": "refund"},
      "graph": {
        "nodes": {
          "submitted": {"type": "trigger"},
          "manager_approval": {
            "type": "approval",
            "contract": {
              "approval": {
                "mode": "any",
                "empty_assignee_policy": "fail",
                "resolvers": [{"type": "role", "role_key": "refund_manager"}]
              }
            }
          },
          "settle": {
            "type": "action",
            "contract": {
              "action": {
                "action_key": "refund.settle",
                "input": {"decision": "approved"},
                "on_error": "fail"
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "edges": {
          "submitted_approval": {"source": "submitted", "target": "manager_approval"},
          "approval_settle": {"source": "manager_approval", "target": "settle", "branch": "approved"}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Workflow, node and edge identities are map keys. Plane injects their internal
identity fields. For an Action node it derives `object_key` from the declared
Action and derives the routed `$record.id` target for record Actions; do not
author either technical field. Node input contains only business parameters.

Approval resolvers are chosen from the business subject: explicit users,
declared role membership, a user-valued record field, `manager_of`, or
`initiator_manager`. `first_match` is ordered fallback; `union` combines all
candidates. Use `empty_assignee_policy: fail` unless bypass/admin fallback is an
accepted business rule.

Graph binding is fail-closed. Every required Action input must come from the
trigger context or a prior node available on every incoming path. Approval wire
decisions are `approved`, `rejected`, and `returned`. A waiting process or open
task is intermediate evidence, not completion.

Acceptance proves resolved assignees, unauthorized decision denial, each
terminal branch, durable process/task state, Handler business effects, retry and
restart resume. Do not replace an expressible graph with one giant Handler or
invent approval tokens and private workflow endpoints.
# Domainry Plane boundary

V2 uses Domainry Plane only through the single packaged `domainry-cli` executable.

Choose one explicit `--environment <local|dev|stage|online>` or `--service <url>` target for `apply model` and Connector definition discovery. Keep that target fixed for the batch.

Release only with:

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> [one target]
```

The command converges `backend/model/*.json`, checks the complete model, validates it with Domainry Plane, publishes the immutable delivery, and materializes or evolves the backend. Source preparation, implementation, tests, and `apply finalize` follow explicitly in the same apply stage. For an existing Builder delivery change, inspect the first run's immutable evolution audit, then rerun the same product command with `--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>`. A stale audit fails closed. Repair any other failed input or stage before rerunning the direct command.

Do not call Domainry Plane directly, reconstruct signing, hand-edit delivery state, or invent separate validate/publish/materialize commands. The current Builder flow keeps reviewed evolution inside `apply model`; it exposes no neighboring delivery-maintenance command surface.
# Project-owned source

Git owns project source. Edit, format, test, rename, and delete in-scope project source with normal development tools while preserving unrelated work. Treat a canonical Handler and its paired test as one review unit and keep both aligned with the same implementation-packet entry. `frontend/**` remains read-only except when an exportable Object SQL Report requires the Data Exchange export center and the TODO says `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; evidence that assigns any other defect to the frontend produces a finding with owner `frontend`, never an edit.

Allowed backend source includes `backend/go.mod`, `backend/go.sum`, `backend/actions/**`, `backend/config/**`, `backend/connectors/**`, `backend/domain/**`, `backend/i18n/**`, and `backend/tests/**`. The sole frontend allowance is the existing project's route/navigation, feature components, typed-client integration, localization, and focused tests needed for the export center in [offline Report export frontend](frontend-offline-report-export.md); do not mutate unrelated frontend source. Never edit `backend/generated/**`, `backend/cmd/**`, frozen contracts, Runtime manifests, receipts, caches, journals, packages, or other `.domainry/**` state. The only writable `.domainry` exception is the current session's `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md` TODO.

## Normal delivered-batch sequence

This is the only source sequence after `apply model` succeeds:

1. Retain the exact `.implementation_packet.path`, delivery/materialization identity, file hash, and returned `actions[]` direct-path index from `apply model`. That command validates every delivered Action context, creates only missing canonical Handler/test skeletons, and persists immutable content-addressed context files under managed `.domainry/builder/**`.
2. For one Action at a time, find its exact `action_key` in the small returned index and read that entry's `path` directly. The file is already the complete single-Action context, including only its referenced document content; do not run `jq`, open the batch index, reconstruct a document table, use `latest.json`, or read generated capabilities/context files directly.
3. Implement the complete Action-context Handler and paired test directly with normal source-editing tools. If either file changed concurrently, stop and reconcile both against the immutable context before continuing.
4. For an approved Connector source gap, load `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project <project> --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementing that Connector under `backend/connectors/**`. Action packet context does not replace Connector context.
5. Implement other allowed project-owned backend source/tests and the authorized export-center exception. Run focused tests, then the affected backend test set.
6. Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project <project>` once all implementation TODO items for the materialized delivery are closed.

There is no second prepare, per-Action context, or source-write command.

The batch-prepared skeleton compiles against delivered capability types but intentionally returns `*.not_implemented`. It exposes missing implementation coverage and is never positive-path evidence. Replace the paired generated test's nil Execution call and placeholder oracle with typed non-nil Execution/capability stubs and assertions over current outputs and business effects; a generic no-panic assertion is not meaningful behavior evidence.

## Finalization boundary

After source/tests are implemented and every preceding implementation TODO item is closed, run the exact generated-SDK-tagged focused Go tests, then `apply finalize`. Finalization scans delivery-bound canonical Action source/test paths. A Handler paired with a generated test that still has nil Execution or an exact `*.not_implemented` oracle returns `state:"invalid"`; source-policy and applicable Go compile failures also fail closed. Finalize writes only its failure receipt on failure. Cross-module/full verification, packaging, and Runtime start require the current successful finalization.

# Authorization and behavior ownership

Keep Action invocation, exact Permission grants, field policy, frontend
navigation, assurance and execution ownership separate.

In backend-model V3:

- the Role's exact `<action_key>;<data_scope>` array entry is the single
  authored Handler allowlist. Never write `Action.roles` or
  `authorization.allowed_roles`; Plane reverse-derives both the allowlist and
  the complete internal authorization contract from Role grants.
- `handler.access` is the minimum Object/operation EffectAuthority. Do not also
  write `handler.data_access`.
- an ordinary Role is an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` strings;
  each Action or CRUD Permission has its own `data_scope`.
- Plane derives the Action Permission definition, reference policies, Handler
  EffectAuthority, behavior tuple and Object write policy. It never invents a
  Role grant or scope value.

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "case_reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner"]
  },
  "actions": {
    "case.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval verifies eligibility and records a durable decision",
        "access": {
          "case": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "case_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Read operations are `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, and
`count`. Write operations are `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`,
`delete`, and `restore`. Locking is not mutation authority. Existing-record
update/delete/restore requires `get_for_update` or `conditional_update`.

Use `object_operation` when no existing record target is supplied and
`record_operation` for a routed record target. Route record ID, workspace,
principal, request, trace and idempotency identities are Runtime/protocol
context and are rejected as Action business input.

A Handler-written Object is `action_only`; its allowed role must explicitly
hold the Handler Action's same-key scoped grant but no direct CRUD permission.
Every other Object is `direct_crud`. Never widen a role or add direct CRUD
merely to satisfy a Handler.

## Scope is an SQL mutation boundary

Treat data-scope enforcement as part of the repository operation, not as
response filtering. `all` means no additional data-scope `WHERE`; workspace,
caller filters and target IDs remain mandatory. Generated reads for `owner`,
`org`, `org_child` and `target_org` must combine the compiled predicate with
those conditions. Existing-record update, delete and restore capabilities must
first select the requested single ID or bounded ID batch with the same scope,
then execute the mutation with that predicate still present in its `UPDATE` or
`DELETE`. Batch target counts must match the authorized selection; any missing
or out-of-scope target fails the whole transaction without partial writes.

Never satisfy scope acceptance by loading unscoped rows and filtering them in
project code. Tests must prove an allowed ID succeeds, an out-of-scope ID is
unchanged, mixed allowed/denied batches roll back atomically, and the repository
query/mutation carries the compiled non-`all` predicate or proves that `all`
contains only workspace, caller-filter and target-ID conditions.

Organization claims are trusted Runtime facts,
not request fields or guessed headers. Sensitive fields remain fail-closed and
their explicit policy comes from the active Authoring Definition.

After implementation, map confirmed PRD authorization boundaries to focused
business-flow tests: actor, target, expected grant/scope, result or denial, and
unchanged durable state after rejection. Use real Identity-backed principals;
Blueprint declarations are not assignment evidence.
# Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract. Frontend dependency installation and package wiring remain outside this Skill except for the authorized Data Exchange export-center integration.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, API facade, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. The authorized export center may wire only typed operations already published by the Application Delivery `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract; a missing Data Exchange job-list operation is a platform-owner gap, never permission to add or guess a route.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/items/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Business-flow tests wrap typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request. For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project <project> --address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. It verifies and packages the project, starts the exact package to healthy state, stops it, restarts the same package/database cohort to healthy state, and finally stops it. A failure triggers best-effort cleanup of any Runtime started by that invocation. If it fails, remain in `verify`, repair the named owner, and rerun the same command. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or add a separate Runtime-control step.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Successful `verify` returns `verified_and_stopped`; a running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, database-cohort, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These are Runtime-facing Handler constraints. `apply finalize` statically checks capability I/O in loops/recursion, bounded List pagination, handled capability results, and each `ConditionalUpdate` call's actual mutation argument. Unit and Runtime tests still own business semantics.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Keep generated capability I/O outside loops and recursive cycles: select into bounded slices, build batch inputs in pure loops, and invoke each generated batch/query capability once. Every List query uses `Page(page, pageSize)` with literal `pageSize` in `1..200`. Handle every result and error. Batch inputs are `1..200`, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's `verify` command supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** Attach the compare-and-set condition observed under `GetForUpdate`; `apply finalize` checks the mutation argument at every call site:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)`, `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)`, and arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects satisfy the generated condition contract. Scaffolded or hand-written fakes must call `ValidateConditionalMutation`. On idempotent replay the predicate may legitimately differ; assert each execution's expected mutation rather than byte equality.

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.
# Offline Report export frontend

Read only when an accepted Object SQL Report requires export and the TODO says `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`.

## Required outcome

Implement one project-level export center using the existing frontend router, navigation, design system, localization, typed Runtime Client, authentication/session handling, error presentation, and test conventions. Reuse an existing export/download center when present; do not create one page per Report.

The user journey is fixed:

1. The Report's Export action submits the Object SQL Report export through the typed Runtime Client.
2. Treat every successful submission as an offline Data Exchange job. Keep the returned job identity and navigate or link to the export center; never expect an immediate file response.
3. The export center obtains the current actor's jobs from the published Data Exchange job-list operation, filtered to `provider=reports` and `operation=export` through typed client parameters.
4. Render the provider-owned projection. Show the Report identity, status, submitted/updated time, progress/row count when supplied, and a stable error state when supplied.
5. Enable Download only for a completed, unexpired job and invoke the published Data Exchange download operation for that job. Preserve the server filename and content type. Enable Cancel only when the typed contract exposes it for the current nonterminal state.

## Security and state rules

- The server-owned actor/workspace filter is authoritative. Do not request another actor's jobs or treat a hidden row/button as authorization.
- Do not query Data Exchange tables, project audit/download Objects, generic Records endpoints, or a locally persisted job-ID collection to synthesize the list.
- Do not build CSV or Blob contents from Report rows in the browser.
- Do not hard-code HTTP paths when the generated Runtime Client publishes the operation.
- Refresh active jobs using the project's existing query/polling conventions and stop refreshing terminal rows. Do not invent WebSocket or notification protocols.
- Preserve empty, loading, stale/retry, failed, cancelled, completed, expired/download-denied, and session-expired states without presenting a queued job as a completed export.

## Contract gap

The page requires a typed Data Exchange job-list operation whose results are actor-owned. If the active capability index or generated Runtime Client exposes only job-by-ID, cancel, and download, record a Data Exchange owner gap and do not implement a fake list from browser memory or internal storage. Keep the Report export submission backend work intact, but leave the frontend slice incomplete until the owner publishes the list contract.

## Verification

Add focused frontend tests using the project's normal test tools:

- export submission creates/navigates to the returned offline job;
- list request uses the published Report-export filter and renders only returned actor-owned jobs;
- active jobs cannot download;
- completed jobs download through the typed Data Exchange operation;
- failed, cancelled, expired/denied, empty, loading, and retry states render truthfully;
- the page does not contain a direct/synchronous CSV path or browser-generated authoritative export.

Run the focused tests and the smallest relevant frontend build/typecheck. Browser visual inspection is required only when the project already has a supported local UI verification path; otherwise report that visual layer as unverified rather than claiming it passed.

The path must be exactly `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`, canonical,
project-local and non-symlink. Plane normalizes line endings, hashes the source
and embeds SQL in the full Runtime contract. `sql_file` and `sql` are mutually
exclusive.

## Empty values and commands

Omit empty strings, arrays and objects. Omit absent `input`, `output`,
`permissions`, `config`, `preconditions` and optional collections; Plane
creates required empty internal structures. `false` and `0` remain legal only
when they are deliberate business values.

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <module> [--allow-destructive]
```

`model plan` is the no-HTTP repair loop. It runs the same loader, Ledger graph,
authoring checks, Project Contract projection, Runtime Manifest compiler and
source-owner validators used by apply. `apply model` atomically converges the
generated Ledger; an item absent from the model is a destructive deletion and
requires `--allow-destructive`.

Capability assembly remains progressive: choose from bounded summaries, load
only selected focused definitions, and let Plane compile ownership, module
closure and digests. Never author or cache a capability assembly in the model.

`templates/backend-model-handler-minimal/model.json.tmpl` is the directly
loadable two-Object Handler starter.

// Approve implements the project-owned conversion_request.approve Handler.
func Approve(ctx context.Context, caps capabilities.ApproveCapabilities, input capabilities.ApproveInput) (capabilities.ApproveOutput, error) {
	_ = input
	request, err := caps.ConversionRequest.GetForUpdate(ctx, caps.Execution.TargetID())
	if err != nil {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, err
	}
	if request.Status != schema.ConversionRequestStatus("pending") {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, &capabilities.BusinessError{Code: "conversion_request.approve.invalid_state"}
	}
	lead, err := caps.Lead.GetForUpdate(ctx, request.LeadID.ID())
	if err != nil {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, err
	}
	if lead.Status != schema.LeadStatus("qualified") {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, &capabilities.BusinessError{Code: "conversion_request.approve.lead_state_conflict"}
	}
	createdCustomer, err := caps.Customer.Create(ctx, schema.CreateCustomer{
		Amount:       schema.CustomerAmount(request.AmountSnapshot),
		CompanyName:  lead.CompanyName,
		ContactName:  lead.ContactName,
		Source:       schema.CustomerSource(lead.Source),
		SourceLeadID: schema.NewCustomerSourceLeadIDReference(lead.ID),
	})
	if err != nil {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, err
	}
	if createdCustomer.ID == "" {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, &capabilities.BusinessError{Code: "conversion_request.approve.empty_customer"}
	}
	now := time.Now().UTC()
	updatedLead, err := caps.Lead.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, data.NewLeadUpdate(lead.ID).
		SetStatus(schema.LeadStatus("converted")).
		SetStatusChangedAt(now).
		RequireStatusEqual(schema.LeadStatus("qualified"), "conversion_request.approve.lead_conflict").
		WithExpectedUpdatedAt(lead.UpdatedAt))
	if err != nil {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, err
	}
	principal := caps.Execution.Principal()
	updatedRequest, err := caps.ConversionRequest.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, data.NewConversionRequestUpdate(request.ID).
		SetStatus(schema.ConversionRequestStatus("approved")).
		SetDecidedAt(now).
		SetDecidedBy(principal.UserID).
		RequireStatusEqual(schema.ConversionRequestStatus("pending"), "conversion_request.approve.conflict").
		WithExpectedUpdatedAt(request.UpdatedAt))
	if err != nil {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, err
	}
	company := lead.CompanyName
	notificationID, err := caps.Notifications.Dispatch(ctx, capabilities.ApproveNotificationIntent{
		EventType:        "lead.conversion_approved",
		SourceEventID:    "conversion-approved:" + string(request.ID),
		RecipientUserIDs: []string{principal.UserID},
		SubjectObjectKey: "lead",
		SubjectRecordID:  string(lead.ID),
		SubjectVersion:   updatedLead.UpdatedAt,
		DedupeKey:        "conversion-approved:" + string(request.ID),
		GroupKey:         "lead:" + string(lead.ID),
		OccurredAt:       now,
		Variables:        []capabilities.ApproveNotificationVariable{{Key: "company_name", StringValue: &company}},
	})
	if err != nil {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, err
	}
	if updatedRequest.ID == "" || notificationID == "" {
		return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, &capabilities.BusinessError{Code: "conversion_request.approve.empty_effect"}
	}
	return capabilities.ApproveOutput{}, nil
}

# Verification evidence levels

Use this ladder for every verification check and final claim. Each level includes the lower levels, but an artifact reaches a level only when its current proof exists and is bound to the current source/model/Runtime identity.

## Ladder

- `L0_declared`: the capability exists in requirements, model metadata, or source. This proves intent only.
- `L1_delivery_verified`: source finalization is current; format, lint, vet, tests, and packaging pass through `verify`. This proves structural/release closure, not behavior.
- `L2_api_verified`: the operation executes through the real managed Runtime with a real session and its durable result is read back through the typed API or database. A denied/error/conflict case proves unchanged durable state; an idempotency case proves one effect after replay.
- `L3_scenario_verified`: every in-scope business-flow case executes end to end on real Runtime data. Each case starts from explicit preconditions, performs the ordered business actions, and observes its terminal durable result; requirement-defined denial, scope and failure branches are included.
- `L4_browser_verified`: reserved for the authorized offline export center when the project already provides a supported local browser verification path. Other browser-layer UI verification remains outside this Skill.
- `L5_restart_verified`: the critical L3 journey subset and sessions remain correct after a managed Runtime restart, with durable state read back and the critical cases rerun.

## Claim rules

- Never call L0/L1 output `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done`; say `declared` or `delivery_verified`.
- Never infer L2/L3 from a test name, source inspection, metadata checklist, `verify`, package receipt, Runtime health, HTTP 2xx alone, TODO prose, or TODO checker success.
- Never count a click, toast, queued job, emitted event, waiting Workflow, metadata-only import/export record, or local state change as the terminal business effect.
- Report skipped checks as skipped. Do not fold them into a higher level.
- Report coverage only with its exact include scope. A subset percentage is not whole-project coverage.
- Treat missing, empty, partial, stale, unbound, contradictory, or hand-written summary evidence as non-passing.

## L3 evidence requirements

For every business-flow case, bind project-local evidence to the current source digest and Runtime delivery identity. Record its requirement/flow ID, test name/path, actor/role, ordered actions, permission and data scope, persistence probe, terminal result, and audit/receipt identity when applicable.

For non-`none` data scope, provide at least two distinguishable owners and two scope groups when the rule separates them, plus records inside and outside the actor's allowed scope. A single actor, team, owner, or record cannot prove a scope boundary.

For mutations:

- success requires different before/after state and a successful read-back;
- denied, validation, and conflict cases require identical before/after state;
- idempotent replay requires the replay state to equal the first successful after-state;
- restart persistence requires the post-restart state to equal the accepted pre-restart state.

## Minimum terminal level

A Delivery Batch requires current L3 for every in-scope business flow and L5 for every changed or affected critical flow marked restart-sensitive. Unchanged flows may reference prior evidence only when it is still bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity; every changed flow and affected regression boundary must reach the same level in the current batch. Whole-product completion may be claimed only when no Requirement ID remains deferred. When the authorized offline export center changes frontend source, its focused tests and smallest relevant build/typecheck are mandatory; reach L4 only when the project already provides a supported local browser path. Other frontend-owned defects remain findings for the frontend owner.
# Business-flow verification and terminal policy

Read this file completely on entry to `verify`, `done`, or terminal review after a repair.

## One verification model

Verification uses project-owned business-flow test cases. There is no acceptance denominator, generic case runner, results JSON protocol, carry-forward/stale-report workflow, or second evidence ledger.

Each current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary has one stable flow ID and one or more ordinary project-owned test cases under `backend/**`. Group cross-module cases under `backend/tests/businessflow/` when that makes ownership clearer; keep focused unit cases beside their source. A flow case starts from explicit preconditions, uses the requirement's real actor and scope, performs the ordered business actions, and asserts the terminal business result through durable read-back. It is not a list of disconnected endpoint checks. An unchanged flow may reuse prior evidence only when the TODO identifies that evidence and proves it remains bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity.

The current-batch business-flow inventory and affected regression closure must cover:

- every current-batch happy path from initial state through all required transitions to its terminal observable result;
- every requirement-defined alternate or rejection branch, including authorization, data-scope, validation and conflict behavior;
- unchanged durable state after a denied, invalid or failed action;
- idempotent replay, transaction rollback, concurrency, restart/resume, notification, schedule, file, integration, Object SQL Report, offline export submission, actor-owned job-list visibility or completed download only when the accepted flow actually depends on it;
- current-batch Requirement ID → Feature key → flow ID → test name/path traceability, plus baseline references for unchanged affected flows.

Do not multiply cases for platform internals that no business requirement observes. One flow case may prove several operations when they are steps of the same business journey. Conversely, do not call a set of isolated unit tests complete when no case executes the required journey end to end.

## Direct commands

Finalize source after focused implementation tests, then run:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` runs the complete backend Go test tree with the delivery's Domain SDK build constraint, packages the verified source, proves an initial healthy start, stops it, proves a healthy restart of the same package/database cohort, and finally stops it. When `backend/tests/businessflow/*_test.go` exists, the CLI compiles that package once from the verified source and runs the same test binary against both healthy Runtime processes before stopping them. Those tests may skip only when `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_URL` is absent during the ordinary pre-package test pass; when present, require `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_PHASE` to be `initial` or `restart` and use the supplied URL. The CLI also supplies immutable delivery, package-receipt, verification-receipt, project-source and database-identity values under the `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_*` prefix. Never start another Runtime or open its database from project tests. Project-owned tests carry the highest-risk and remaining business-flow oracles; the CLI owns structural, package and lifecycle proof. Record the command, test paths, package/Runtime/database identities, and concise result in the current TODO.

Do not generate a separate coverage denominator or duplicate result files. The traceability table in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`, the project test inventory, `verify` receipt and current TODO are the complete verification record.

Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque values returned by formal APIs. A `2xx`, process health response, emitted event, queued job, toast, empty collection or local state change is not a terminal business result unless the accepted requirement says it is. Mutations require durable read-back; negative cases require the intended error and unchanged state.

Finish the complete reachable flow round before repair so the finding inventory is useful. Repair the named owner, rerun focused tests, then rerun affected business-flow cases plus `verify` when source identity changed. Do not invent workflow metadata or a parallel state machine.

## Terminal state

`done` requires all current-batch business flows and affected regression boundaries to have current passing cases, the highest-risk changed real Runtime flow to pass, structural verification and package receipts to be current, and the batch finding inventory to be empty. It closes only the Delivery Batch; whole-product completion additionally requires an empty deferred Requirement inventory. A genuinely unavailable external provider may be reported as `verification_blocked` only after every authorized local or sandbox route is exhausted; an ordinary failed case remains a repair finding. Successful CLI verification ends in `verified_and_stopped` with no managed Runtime intentionally left running.

Before completion, keep `Current stage: verify`. Change it to `done` only after the policy above is satisfied and the TODO evidence points to current CLI receipts and Runtime observations.

When the authorized offline export center is in scope, verification also runs its focused frontend tests and smallest relevant build/typecheck, and uses the project's supported browser verification path when available. Prove loading, empty, active, completed/downloadable, failed, cancelled, expired/denied, and cross-actor isolation states without treating a queued job as terminal. If the typed Data Exchange job-list operation is absent, keep the slice incomplete as an owner gap rather than substituting browser memory.

The final summary states the Delivery Batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, current-batch and affected-regression test results, managed Runtime result, focused export-center frontend result when applicable, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations. Unrelated browser-layer UI verification remains outside this Skill.

# Backend Runtime integration and managed proof

This reference covers the closed Runtime HTTP boundary, Action invocation, managed Runtime proof, and backend Handler coding idioms. Capability discovery comes from the CLI-compiled authority contract. Frontend dependency installation and package wiring remain outside this Skill except for the authorized Data Exchange export-center integration.

## Closed HTTP boundary

Project-owned backend source must not add, register, proxy, or require any application-facing HTTP interface. Do not create a project-local HTTP handler, router, controller, middleware endpoint, API facade, API proxy, serverless function, or alternate transport route. The authorized export center may wire only typed operations already published by the Application Delivery `runtime-domain-api-v1` contract; a missing Data Exchange job-list operation is a platform-owner gap, never permission to add or guess a route.

Custom source-owned Action Handlers expose no separate HTTP route; Runtime invokes them only through the published object or record Action operations below. Connector providers may perform contract-declared outbound calls through generated Connector APIs and governed transport, but they must not publish an inbound project API. If the published Runtime CRUD, Action, Report, file, authentication, or Connector contracts cannot express a required behavior, record the exact platform-owner finding and repair that owner in the same session instead of adding an HTTP endpoint; only the terminal policy's proved unrecoverable conditions permit stopping.

## Action invocation

Select object versus record invocation from the Runtime-published Action `kind`, using `runtimeActionInvocationScope`; never infer it from UI layout or from whether the execution owner is a custom Handler.

- `object_create`, `object_operation`, and `bulk_operation` use `runObjectAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/actions/{actionKey}`.
- `record_update`, `record_delete`, `record_restore`, `transition_state`, `conditional_update`, and `record_operation` use `runRecordAction` at `POST /records/{objectKey}/items/{recordID}/actions/{actionKey}`.

Business-flow tests wrap typed Action input as `{"data": <payload>}`; a bare payload is invalid for the Action invocation contract.

Call `listActions(objectKey)` first and pass the returned full `action_definition.key` unchanged to `runObjectAction` or `runRecordAction`; never shorten `group_class.book_group_class` to `book_group_class`. Use the exact storage values published by the Action input contract, such as `member`, not translated labels such as `会员`. A `record_operation` also requires the existing record ID in the record route; the presence of a button on an object list does not turn it into an object Action.

Frontends never call a generated Handler directly. Preserve the bounded Action input/output contract, workspace, bearer identity, request ID, idempotency key, assurance token, and concurrency value. Preserve Runtime result references and triggered workflows instead of reducing the response to a success boolean.

One accepted business intent must produce one Runtime mutation request. For example, “open table” is one declared Action call, not `create table session` followed by separate status, occupancy, audit, and notification mutations. Do not use `Promise.all`, sequential mutation hooks, retries with new keys, or a browser-side rollback to assemble one atomic backend command. Put the complete typed input on the Action and let its Runtime-owned unit of work perform all effects. Refetch/invalidation after the response and polling a returned job are allowed reads; they must not hide additional writes.

## Managed Runtime proof

Run `"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project <project> --address 127.0.0.1:<dedicated-port>`. It verifies and packages the project, starts the exact package to healthy state, stops it, restarts the same package/database cohort to healthy state, and finally stops it. A failure triggers best-effort cleanup of any Runtime started by that invocation. If it fails, remain in `verify`, repair the named owner, and rerun the same command. Never background-launch, discover arbitrary PIDs, kill unrelated processes, or add a separate Runtime-control step.

Runtime proof must cover declared allowed, denied, and scoped actors; Action effects; conditional conflicts; transaction rollback; idempotent replay without a second mutation or receipt; workflows/outbox; durable audit; and current delivery/package/Runtime receipt identity. Use task-published database evidence paths; do not rediscover private schema.

Successful `verify` returns `verified_and_stopped`; a running process, local HTTP response, or browser screenshot without matching delivery, package, database-cohort, and Runtime identity is not release evidence.

## Handler coding idioms (validated against the live Runtime)

These are Runtime-facing Handler constraints. `apply finalize` statically checks capability I/O in loops/recursion, bounded List pagination, handled capability results, and each `ConditionalUpdate` call's actual mutation argument. Unit and Runtime tests still own business semantics.

**Finalizer source-contract preflight.** Keep generated capability I/O outside loops and recursive cycles: select into bounded slices, build batch inputs in pure loops, and invoke each generated batch/query capability once. Every List query uses `Page(page, pageSize)` with literal `pageSize` in `1..200`. Handle every result and error. Batch inputs are `1..200`, ordered one-to-one, and inherit the Action Workspace, Principal, grants, Scope, and transaction. Minimal shape:

```go
// Pure selection: capability I/O only outside loops.
orders, err := caps.RepairOrder.List(ctx, data.NewRepairOrderQuery().
    WhereStatusEqual(schema.RepairOrderStatusDispatched).
    OrderByIDAscending().
    Page(1, 200)) // literal page size, 1..200
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
pending := make([]schema.RepairOrder, 0, runCapacity)
for _, order := range orders { // pure filtering loop: no capability calls here
    if len(pending) == runCapacity {
        break
    }
    if eligible(order) {
        pending = append(pending, order)
    }
}
queries := make([]data.DispatchReceiptQuery, len(pending))
for index, order := range pending { // pure request construction only
    queries[index] = data.NewDispatchReceiptQuery().
        WhereOrderIDEqual(order.ID).
        WhereBusinessDateEqual(businessDate)
}
exists, err := caps.DispatchReceipt.ExistsBatch(ctx, queries) // one call, outside loops
if err != nil {
    return out, err
}
// Build CreateBatch and notification DispatchBatch inputs in pure loops, then
// invoke each batch once outside loops and return every error unchanged.
```

**Build tag.** Backend compile requires the Domain SDK build constraint: a plain `go build ./...` fails on `verifiedDomainSDKBuildConstraint`. The tag is published as `schema.DomainSDKBuildConstraint` in the generated schema package's revision constants; run all backend commands as `go build|vet|test -tags "$(go run ./cmd/... 2>/dev/null || grep -roh 'domainry_domain_sdk_[a-f0-9]*' backend/generated/ | head -1)" ./...` — or read the constant from `backend/generated/schema/revision.gen.go`. The CLI's `verify` command supplies the tag automatically; only manual Go commands need it.

**ConditionalUpdate requires a real condition.** Attach the compare-and-set condition observed under `GetForUpdate`; `apply finalize` checks the mutation argument at every call site:

```go
mutation := data.NewTicketUpdate(ticket.ID).SetAssigneeID(assignee)
if ticket.AssigneeID == nil {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDNull("ticket.assign.conflict")
} else {
    mutation = mutation.RequireAssigneeIDEqual(*ticket.AssigneeID, "ticket.assign.conflict")
}
updated, err := caps.Ticket.ConditionalUpdate(ctx, mutation)
```

`Require<Field>Equal/NotEqual/Null(errorCode)`, `WithExpectedUpdatedAt(...)`, and arithmetic `Increment*`/`Decrement*` effects satisfy the generated condition contract. Scaffolded or hand-written fakes must call `ValidateConditionalMutation`. On idempotent replay the predicate may legitimately differ; assert each execution's expected mutation rather than byte equality.

**NotificationIntent.SubjectVersion must be non-empty.** `runtimeext.NotificationIntent` fails `backend.notification.action_intent_invalid` when `SubjectVersion` is empty. Generated typed reads and mutation results expose `UpdatedAt`; mutation results receive it from the same canonical staged commit that Runtime persists. Use the subject record's `UpdatedAt` (including the value returned by `ConditionalUpdate`) as `SubjectVersion`; do not substitute transport metadata such as `request_id`, leave the field empty, or skip the dispatch.

**Transition Actions from Handlers or probes** must send the target state in the request payload (see `crud-and-state-machine.md`): a payload-less transition fails closed with 400 `backend.action.transition_payload_required`.

# M1 Benchmark:销售线索 CRM 需求规格

本文档是 benchmark 的唯一需求输入。评分对照 golden-checklist(agent 不可见)。

## 业务背景

一家 B2B 公司的销售团队管理线索(lead)到成交客户(customer)的全流程:销售录入并跟进线索,大额转化需销售总监审批,团队按部门划分数据边界,管理层看漏斗报表并导出。

## 组织与角色

- 销售分属**部门**(至少两个部门:华东区、华北区),存在汇报线。
- **sales_rep(销售)**:录入/跟进自己名下的线索;可见范围=本部门线索;发起转化。
- **sales_director(销售总监)**:全部门可见;审批大额转化;查看/导出漏斗报表。

## 功能需求

### 线索管理
1. 线索字段:公司名(必填)、联系人、联系电话、预计金额(精确金额,两位小数)、来源(select:官网/展会/转介绍/外呼)、状态、负责人(销售)、部门、创建/更新时间。
2. 线索状态机:`new → contacted → qualified → converted / lost`;`qualified` 可标记 `lost`;`converted`、`lost` 为终态,不可再转换。
3. 销售创建线索(初始 new,负责人=本人,部门=本人部门);可更新自己名下线索的联系人/电话/预计金额/来源。
4. 跟进(contacted)与合格判定(qualified)由负责人执行;状态只能沿定义的转换变化。
5. 线索创建幂等(相同幂等键重复提交只建一条)。

### 转化与审批(核心业务)
6. 负责人对 `qualified` 线索发起**转化**:预计金额 < 100000 时直接转化;≥ 100000 时必须进入**审批流**,由 sales_director 审批。
7. 审批通过:线索进入 `converted`,并在**同一事务**中创建 `customer` 客户记录(承接公司名/联系人/金额/来源线索引用);审批拒绝:线索回到 `qualified` 并记录拒绝原因。
8. 转化必须幂等:同一线索重复发起转化不产生第二个客户。
9. 审批结果(通过/拒绝)以站内通知发给发起的销售。
10. 客户记录只读(任何角色不可更新/删除客户;修正走新流程,本期不做)。

### 数据边界
11. 销售的线索可见范围 = **本部门**(同部门同事的线索可见,跨部门不可见);更新/状态操作仅限**自己名下**。
12. 总监全量可见。
13. 所有状态变化与转化审批留审计。

### 跟进提醒(定时)
14. 每天早上(工作日)由**定时任务**扫描:`contacted` 状态超过 7 天未变化的线索,给负责人发站内提醒(每条线索每天最多提醒一次)。

### 报表与导出
15. 总监可见**漏斗报表**:按状态统计线索数与预计金额合计;销售无权查看。
16. 总监可**导出线索明细 CSV**(带当前权限过滤);导出必须走受控导出通道(有界、审计、requester 专属)。
17. 线索列表服务端有界分页。

### 导航与验收
18. 两角色登录 Business Workspace 后菜单与权限一致(销售:我的线索;总监:全部线索、报表)。
19. 提供两个部门 × 各 1 名销售 + 1 名总监的非人类验收身份,以及覆盖所有状态、两个部门、含 ≥100000 与 <100000 金额的种子线索(≥6 条),保证每条需求可在真实 Runtime 验证。

## 范围限定

仅 Business Workspace;无 Consumer Portal、无外部连接器;金额计算只做求和,不涉及分成/结算。

## 公开业务旅程追踪 ID

以下 ID 是需求输入的一部分，不包含 evaluator 的隐藏断言。`docs/backend-requirements-prd.md`
必须建立需求 → flow ID → 测试名/路径追踪；`backend/tests/businessflow/` 下对应的顶层 Go 测试名
必须以 `TestBFxx` 开头。同一 ID 可以拆成多个测试，但每个分支都要验证持久化终态和失败后的状态不变性。

- `BF01`：销售创建线索、创建幂等、本人更新、负责人状态推进，以及同部门非负责人写入拒绝。
- `BF02`：小额线索从 qualified 直接转化、只创建一个只读客户，并验证重放幂等。

type identityUserProvisioningResponse struct {
	identitymodel.IdentityUser
	InitialPassword    string `json:"initial_password"`
	MustChangePassword bool   `json:"must_change_password"`
}

func (h *IdentityHandler) listIdentityUsers(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	users, err := h.users.ListUsersWithinDataScope(r.Context(), h.principal(r), "identity.users.list")
	if err != nil {
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	h.writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, users)
}

func (h *IdentityHandler) searchIdentityUsers(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	page, err := h.users.SearchUsersWithinDataScope(r.Context(), identityListQuery(r), h.principal(r), "identity.users.search")
	if err != nil {
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	h.writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, page)
}

func (h *IdentityHandler) searchIdentityAccounts(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	if batch, ok := h.userSecurity.(IdentityUserSecurityBatch); ok {
		page, err := h.users.SearchUserProjectionBatchWithinDataScope(r.Context(), identityListQuery(r), h.principal(r), "identity.accounts.search", func(ctx context.Context, workspaceID string, userIDs []string) (map[string]identityapplication.IdentityUserProjectionSecuritySummary, error) {
			profiles, readErr := batch.UserProjectionSecurityProfiles(ctx, workspaceID, userIDs)
			if readErr != nil {
				return nil, readErr
			}
			summaries := make(map[string]identityapplication.IdentityUserProjectionSecuritySummary, len(profiles))
			for userID, profile := range profiles {
				lastLoginAt := ""
				if profile.Credential != nil {
					lastLoginAt = profile.Credential.LastLoginAt
				}
				summaries[userID] = identityapplication.IdentityUserProjectionSecuritySummary{
					MFAEnabled: profile.MFAEnabled, Locked: profile.Locked, ActiveSessions: profile.ActiveSessions, LastLoginAt: lastLoginAt,
				}
			}
			return summaries, nil
		})
		if err != nil {
			h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
			return
		}
		h.writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, page)
		return
	}
	page, err := h.users.SearchUserProjectionWithinDataScope(r.Context(), identityListQuery(r), h.principal(r), "identity.accounts.search", func(ctx context.Context, workspaceID, userID string) (identityapplication.IdentityUserProjectionSecuritySummary, error) {
		profile, readErr := h.userSecurity.UserSecurityProfile(ctx, workspaceID, userID)
		if readErr != nil {
			return identityapplication.IdentityUserProjectionSecuritySummary{}, readErr
		}
		lastLoginAt := ""
		if profile.Credential != nil {
			lastLoginAt = profile.Credential.LastLoginAt
		}
		return identityapplication.IdentityUserProjectionSecuritySummary{
			MFAEnabled: profile.MFAEnabled, Locked: profile.Locked,
			ActiveSessions: profile.ActiveSessions, LastLoginAt: lastLoginAt,
		}, nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	h.writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, page)
}

func (h *IdentityHandler) getIdentityUser(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	user, found, err := h.users.UserByIDWithinDataScope(r.Context(), strings.TrimSpace(r.PathValue("userID")), h.principal(r), "identity.users.get")
	if err != nil {
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	if !found {
		h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusNotFound, "backend.identity.user_not_found")
		return
	}
	h.writeIdentityAuthoringResource(w, r, "identity.user", user.ID, user)
}

func (h *IdentityHandler) createIdentityUser(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var user identitymodel.IdentityUser
	if !h.decodeJSON(w, r, &user) {
		return
	}
	user.ID = strings.TrimSpace(user.ID)
	principal := h.principal(r)
	if err := h.users.CreateUserWithinDataScope(r.Context(), user, principal, "identity.users.create"); err != nil {
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	persisted, found, err := h.users.UserByIDWithinDataScope(r.Context(), user.ID, principal, "identity.users.create")
	if err != nil {
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	if !found {
		h.writeError(w, r, http.StatusInternalServerError, "backend.identity.user_not_found")
		return
	}
	if h.userSecurity == nil {
		_ = h.users.RemoveUser(r.Context(), user.ID)
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, apperror.New(
			apperror.KindInternal,
			"backend.identity.initial_credential_issuer_unavailable",
			nil,
			map[string]string{"user": user.ID},
		))
		return
	}
	initialPassword, err := h.userSecurity.IssueInitialPassword(
		r.Context(),
		h.principal(r).WorkspaceID,
		user.ID,
	)
	if err != nil {
		_ = h.users.RemoveUser(r.Context(), user.ID)
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	h.appendIdentityMutationAudit(r, "identity_user_created", "identity_user", user.ID, "Created identity user", map[string]any{"email": user.Email, "status": user.Status})
	w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-store")
	w.Header().Set("Pragma", "no-cache")
	h.writeJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, identityUserProvisioningResponse{
		IdentityUser:       persisted,
		InitialPassword:    initialPassword,
		MustChangePassword: true,
	})
}

func (h *IdentityHandler) updateIdentityUser(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var user identitymodel.IdentityUser
	if !h.decodeJSON(w, r, &user) {
		return
	}
	user.ID = valueOrDefault(strings.TrimSpace(r.PathValue("userID")), user.ID)
	principal := h.principal(r)
	result, err := h.executeIdentityAuthoringUpsert(r.Context(), "identity.user", user.ID, r.Header.Get("Builder-Task-ID"), r.Header.Get("Idempotency-Key"), r.Header.Get("Expected-Schema-Hash"), user, principal,
		func(ctx context.Context) (any, bool, error) {
			return h.users.UserByIDWithinDataScope(ctx, user.ID, principal, "identity.users.update")
		},
		func(ctx context.Context) (any, error) {
			if executeErr := h.users.UpdateUserWithinDataScope(ctx, user, principal, "identity.users.update"); executeErr != nil {
				return nil, executeErr
			}
			h.appendIdentityMutationAudit(r, "identity_user_updated", "identity_user", user.ID, "Updated identity user", map[string]any{"email": user.Email, "status": user.Status})
			persisted, found, readErr := h.users.UserByIDWithinDataScope(ctx, user.ID, principal, "identity.users.update")
			if readErr != nil {
				return nil, readErr
			}
			if !found {
				return nil, &apperror.AppError{Kind: apperror.KindInternal, Code: "backend.identity.user_not_found"}
			}
			return persisted, nil
		})
	h.writeIdentityAuthoringResult(w, r, http.StatusOK, result, err)
}

}

func (h *IdentityHandler) removeIdentityUserRole(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	userID := strings.TrimSpace(r.PathValue("userID"))
	roleID := strings.TrimSpace(r.PathValue("roleID"))
	principal := h.principal(r)
	reason := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("reason"))
	if err := h.roles.RemoveUserRoleGoverned(r.Context(), userID, roleID, reason, principal); err != nil {
		h.securityPrincipal(r, principal, "identity_entitlement_revocation_denied", "Denied identity entitlement revocation", map[string]any{
			"target_user_id": userID, "role_id": roleID, "error_code": apperror.CodeOf(err),
		})
		h.writeServiceError(w, r, err)
		return
	}
	h.appendIdentityMutationAudit(r, "identity_user_role_removed", "identity_user", userID, "Removed identity role from user", map[string]any{"role_id": roleID, "reason": valueOrDefault(reason, "manual_removal")})
	w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNoContent)
}
